title: Hamiltonian simulation with product formulas
summary: Turn simple term evolutions into an approximation of a sum Hamiltonian.
why: The first concrete route from a Hamiltonian description to executable time evolution.
advantage: Theoretical simulation guarantees; practical advantage depends on structure and output.

title: Randomized simulation and qDRIFT
summary: Sample Hamiltonian terms while distinguishing a channel average from one random circuit.
why: Introduces randomized simulation and the essential pure-state versus mixture distinction.
advantage: Proven channel-error bound under term access; comparative benefit is instance-dependent.

title: Energy estimation and ground-state preparation
summary: Turn time-evolution phases into energies and expose the cost of initial overlap.
why: Connects phase estimation and simulation to a central scientific use case.
advantage: Theoretical conditional guarantees; overlap, gap and simulation access can dominate.

title: HHL: a complete two-equation example
summary: Label eigenvalues, rotate a reciprocal flag, uncompute, and check against classical inversion.
why: Makes state-output linear solving and postselection costs explicit before modern abstractions.
advantage: Conditional advantage in sparse/coherent access models; no generic full-vector speedup.

title: Block encoding and linear combinations of unitaries
summary: Embed a scaled matrix in a larger unitary with a visible success branch.
why: Provides the shared input representation for modern matrix algorithms.
advantage: Primitive; speedup is meaningful only after constructing access and specifying an application.

title: Oblivious amplitude amplification
summary: Amplify an encoded unitary without knowing the system input.
why: Explains when ancilla-only reflections work and when they distort a nonunitary map.
advantage: Proven coherent amplification under unitary or controlled near-unitary block promises.

title: Taylor-series and LCU Hamiltonian simulation
summary: Construct a finite exponential polynomial and account for truncation and amplification.
why: Shows a simulation strategy with improved precision dependence and its interaction-picture extension.
advantage: Proven term-access simulation bounds; toy LCU does not claim a scalable implementation.

title: Qubitization: eigenvalues become rotations
summary: Calculate the invariant two-dimensional plane and its Chebyshev response.
why: Links Hamiltonian access, quantum walks, and polynomial transformations.
advantage: Proven oracle-model construction; not itself a physical time-evolution operator.

title: Quantum signal processing
summary: Use a phase sequence to change a signal-dependent amplitude polynomial.
why: Makes the mechanism and admissibility constraints behind modern matrix transformations visible.
advantage: Proven polynomial synthesis framework with access and phase-computation costs.

title: Quantum singular value transformation
summary: Compute a non-Hermitian cubic through a complete four-dimensional unitary.
why: Generalizes eigenvalue transformations while distinguishing singular-value polynomials from ordinary powers.
advantage: Proven oracle-model framework; end-to-end benefit depends on application promises.

title: Modern quantum linear-system solvers
summary: Invert a two-point spectrum with a tested Chebyshev/LCU construction.
why: Explains improvements beyond HHL without erasing conditioning, access or readout costs.
advantage: Conditional access-model speedups; optimal query bounds are not full-runtime claims.

title: Polynomial filtering and ground/thermal preparation
summary: Compare ground-state selection with preparation of a genuinely mixed Gibbs state.
why: Covers overlap, gap, thermal normalization and the QET-U access-model extension.
advantage: Theoretical conditional guarantees; arbitrary ground or Gibbs preparation is not efficient.

title: Singular-value estimation and quantum PCA
summary: Separate block, row-state and copy-access models with a calculated partial-SWAP step.
why: Prevents conflating matrix algorithms and quantum-data PCA or hiding data-loading/copy costs.
advantage: Access-model-dependent theoretical advantages; classical sampling methods change some comparisons.

title: Quantum algorithms for differential equations
summary: Encode a time history as a linear system and calculate final-time extraction cost.
why: Connects matrix algorithms to nonunitary dynamics while exposing discretization, norm and readout costs.
advantage: Conditional theoretical speedups for specified stable/access models; no general nonlinear claim.

title: Quantum semidefinite programming
summary: Work a Gibbs update, then derive a general feasibility loop, stopping certificate and measurement budget.
why: Connects Gibbs-state primitives to constrained matrix optimization with explicit output restrictions.
advantage: Oracle-model speedups with norm, sparsity and precision factors; practical advantage unestablished.
